title: the experiences, attitudes, and opinions of oncology patients at CCC-LMU regarding the digital stress screening to assess support needs and the early integration of palliative care services
summary:
In cancer medicine, palliative care—i.e., care that alleviates symptoms and improves well-being—has been used very differently and often rather late in the treatment process. A new approach aims to connect patients with a palliative care team when certain symptoms or stresses arise. Indications of this can come from short (digital) questionnaires in which those affected indicate their symptoms and their need for support.

Several large cancer centers in Germany are currently testing this approach. However, little is known so far about how patients experience and evaluate this type of early, symptom-based care and the use of digital tools.

In order to find out how those affected experience this form of care, interviews are conducted with patients from various medical fields. Participants are selected according to clearly defined criteria, such as gender, age, type of cancer, whether they are treated on an outpatient basis or in hospital, and their current level of discomfort (measured using the short IPOS-6 questionnaire).

The interviews follow a semi-structured interview guide. This means that there are fixed topics and questions, but at the same time enough space for respondents to freely report on their experiences and attitudes – both regarding digital screening and possible subsequent contact with the palliative care team.

The interviews are evaluated using an established method of qualitative content analysis according to Kuckartz. The statements are systematically sorted, organized by topic, and interpreted. This process is supported by MAXQDA software, which helps to clearly structure large amounts of text material.
conditions: patients' perspectives on symptom- or stress-driven access to palliative care services

interventions.name: Qualitative interview study with patients from various oncological departments at CCC-LMU who participated in digital screening for stress and support needs

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
‐  Patients with solid tumors or malignant hematological neoplasms
- Participation in digital stress screening
- Day clinic or inpatient oncological treatment at LMU Hospital
Exclusion criteria:
‐ Patients who do not have a sufficient understanding of written and spoken German
‐ Patients who are younger than 18 years of age
‐ Patients who, in the opinion of the attending physicians, are too stressed by the overall situation or illness
‐ Acute or chronic qualitative or quantitative impairment of consciousness (e.g., delirium, advanced dementia, neurological impairment due to underlying disease), which prevents a valid interview from being conducted
